verses.1:1: Love righteousness, you who judge the earth; think of the Lord with goodness, and in singleness of heart seek Him.
verses.1:2: For He is found by those who do not put Him to the test, and manifests Himself to those who do not distrust Him.
verses.1:3: For crooked reasonings separate from God, and His power, when put to the test, reproves the foolish.
verses.1:4: For wisdom shall not enter a soul that devises evil, nor dwell in a body indebted to sin.
verses.1:5: For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and will withdraw from senseless thoughts, and will be repelled when unrighteousness approaches.
verses.1:6: For wisdom is a spirit that loves mankind, yet will not acquit a blasphemer for his lips; for God is a witness of his inward parts, a true overseer of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
verses.1:7: For the Spirit of the Lord has filled the world, and that which holds all things together has knowledge of speech.
verses.1:8: Therefore no one who utters unrighteous things shall escape notice, nor indeed shall justice, when it convicts, pass him by.
verses.1:9: For inquiry shall be made into the counsels of the ungodly, and the report of his words shall come to the Lord for the conviction of his lawless deeds.
verses.1:10: For a jealous ear listens to all things, and the sound of murmurings is not hidden.
verses.1:11: Guard yourselves therefore against unprofitable murmuring, and spare your tongue from slander; for a secret utterance shall not go forth in vain, and a lying mouth slays the soul.
verses.1:12: Do not invite death in the error of your life, nor draw destruction upon yourselves by the works of your hands;
verses.1:13: for God did not make death, nor does He delight in the destruction of the living.
verses.1:14: For He created all things that they might exist, and the generations of the world are wholesome, and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor is the dominion of Hades upon the earth;
verses.1:16: But the ungodly by their hands and words summoned him; considering him a friend, they wasted away, and they made a covenant with him, because they are worthy to belong to his portion.
verses.2:1: For they said among themselves, reasoning unsoundly: "Short and sorrowful is our life, and there is no remedy at the end of a man, and no one has been known who returned from Hades.
verses.2:2: For we were born by mere chance, and hereafter we shall be as though we had never existed; for the breath in our nostrils is smoke, and reason is a spark in the beating of our heart,
verses.2:3: which being extinguished, the body shall turn to ashes, and the spirit shall be dispersed like empty air.
verses.2:4: And our name shall be forgotten in time, and no one shall remember our works; and our life shall pass away like the traces of a cloud, and shall be scattered like a mist, driven away by the rays of the sun and weighed down by its heat.
verses.2:5: For our life is the passing of a shadow, and there is no turning back of our end; for it has been sealed, and no one returns.
verses.2:6: Come therefore, and let us enjoy the good things that exist, and let us use creation eagerly as in youth.
verses.2:7: Let us take our fill of costly wine and perfumes, and let no flower of the air pass us by;
verses.2:8: let us crown ourselves with rosebuds before they wither;
verses.2:9: let none of us be without a share in our revelry; everywhere let us leave behind tokens of our gladness, for this is our portion, and this is our lot.
verses.2:10: Let us oppress the righteous poor man; let us not spare the widow, nor show reverence for the gray hairs of the aged of many years.
verses.2:11: But let our might be the law of righteousness, for that which is weak is proved useless.
verses.2:12: Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he is troublesome to us, and opposes our works, and reproaches us for sins against the law, and charges us with sins against our upbringing.
verses.2:13: He professes to have knowledge of God, and calls himself a child of the Lord.
verses.2:14: He has become to us a reproof of our thoughts;
verses.2:15: he is grievous to us even to look upon, because his life is unlike that of others, and his paths are different.
verses.2:16: We are counted by him as counterfeit, and he keeps away from our ways as from uncleanness; he calls the end of the righteous blessed, and boasts that God is his Father.
verses.2:17: Let us see if his words are true, and let us test what shall happen at his departure.
verses.2:18: For if the righteous man is a son of God, He will uphold him, and will deliver him from the hand of those who oppose him.
verses.2:19: Let us examine him with outrage and torment, that we may know his gentleness and judge his forbearance.
verses.2:20: Let us condemn him to a shameful death, for there shall be a visitation for him according to his words."
verses.2:21: These things they reasoned, and they were led astray; for their own wickedness blinded them, and they did not know the mysteries
verses.2:22: of Him, nor did they hope for the wages of holiness, nor did they discern the prize of blameless souls.
verses.2:23: For God created man for incorruption, and made him the image of His own nature;
verses.2:24: but through the envy of the devil death entered into the world, and those who belong to his portion experience it.
verses.3:1: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and torment shall by no means touch them.
verses.3:2: In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died,
verses.3:3: and their departure was reckoned as affliction, and their going from us as destruction; but they are in peace.
verses.3:4: For even if in the sight of men they are punished, their hope is full of immortality;
verses.3:5: and having been chastened a little, they shall receive great good, because God tested them and found them worthy of Himself.
verses.3:6: Like gold in a smelting furnace He proved them, and like a whole burnt sacrifice He accepted them.
verses.3:7: And in the time of their visitation they shall shine forth, and they shall run like sparks through the stubble.
verses.3:8: They shall judge nations and have dominion over peoples, and the Lord shall reign over them forever.
verses.3:9: Those who trust in Him shall understand truth, and the faithful shall abide with Him in love, because grace and mercy are for His chosen ones.
verses.3:10: But the ungodly shall receive punishment according to what they reasoned, who disregarded the righteous man and turned away from the Lord.
verses.3:11: For wretched is he who despises wisdom and discipline; their hope is empty, their labors are unprofitable, and their works are useless.
verses.3:12: Their wives are foolish, and their children are wicked;
verses.3:13: cursed is their offspring. For blessed is the barren woman who is undefiled, who has not known a bed in transgression; she shall have fruit in the visitation of souls.
verses.3:14: And blessed is the eunuch who has worked no lawless deed with his hand, nor thought evil things against the Lord; for to him shall be given a choice favor for his faithfulness, and a more pleasing lot in the temple of the Lord.
verses.3:15: For the fruit of good labors is glorious, and the root of understanding does not fail.
verses.3:16: But the children of adulterers shall not come to maturity, and the seed of an unlawful bed shall vanish away.
verses.3:17: For even if they live long, they shall be counted as nothing, and at the last their old age shall be without honor.
verses.3:18: And if they die swiftly, they have no hope, nor consolation in the day of decision.
verses.3:19: For grievous are the ends of an unrighteous generation.
verses.4:1: Better is childlessness with virtue, for immortality is in the remembrance of it, because it is acknowledged both before God and before men.
verses.4:2: When it is present, men imitate it, and when it has departed, they long for it; and throughout eternity it marches in triumph wearing a crown, having won the contest for undefiled prizes.
verses.4:3: But the prolific multitude of the ungodly will be of no profit, and from illegitimate shoots it will not strike a deep root, nor establish a secure foundation.
verses.4:4: For even if they flourish in branches for a season, standing unsteadily, they will be shaken by the wind, and by the violence of winds they will be uprooted.
verses.4:5: Immature twigs will be snapped off, and their fruit will be useless, unripe for eating and fit for nothing.
verses.4:6: For children born of unlawful unions are witnesses of wickedness against their parents at their examination.
verses.4:7: But the righteous man, though he die before his time, shall be at rest.
verses.4:8: For honorable old age is not one of long duration, nor is it measured by the number of years.
verses.4:9: Rather, understanding is gray hair for men, and an unblemished life is ripe old age.
verses.4:10: Having become well-pleasing to God, he was loved, and while living among sinners, he was taken away.
verses.4:11: He was caught away, lest wickedness alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul.
verses.4:12: For the bewitchment of baseness obscures what is good, and the roving of desire undermines an innocent mind.
verses.4:13: Having been perfected in a short time, he fulfilled long years.
verses.4:14: For his soul was pleasing to the Lord; therefore it hastened out of the midst of wickedness.
verses.4:15: Yet the peoples saw and did not understand, nor did they lay such a thing to heart: that grace and mercy are with His chosen ones, and watchful care is with His holy ones.
verses.4:16: But the righteous man who has died will condemn the ungodly who are still living, and youth quickly perfected will condemn the long old age of the unrighteous.
verses.4:17: For they will see the end of the wise man, and will not understand what He purposed concerning him, or for what end the Lord kept him safe.
verses.4:19: They will see and despise him, but the Lord will laugh them to scorn; and after this they shall become a dishonored corpse and an object of reproach among the dead forever. For He will dash them headlong, speechless, and shake them from their foundations; to the uttermost they shall be laid waste, and they shall be in anguish, and their remembrance shall perish.
verses.4:20: They will come in dread at the reckoning of their sins, and their lawless deeds will convict them to their face.
verses.5:1: Then the righteous man will stand with great boldness before the face of those who afflicted him and of those who made light of his labors.
verses.5:2: When they see him, they will be shaken with dreadful fear, and they will be astounded at the unexpectedness of salvation.
verses.5:3: They will say among themselves in repentance, and through anguish of spirit they will groan, "This was the one whom we once held in derision and as a byword of reproach,
verses.5:4: we fools! We accounted his life to be madness, and his end without honor.
verses.5:5: How has he been numbered among the sons of God, and how is his lot among the saints?
verses.5:6: Surely we have strayed from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness did not shine upon us, and the sun did not rise for us.
verses.5:7: We had our fill in the paths of lawlessness and destruction, and we journeyed through trackless deserts, but the way of the Lord we did not know.
verses.5:8: What has arrogance profited us? And what has wealth with boasting brought to us?
verses.5:9: All those things have passed away like a shadow, and like a message hurrying by;
verses.5:10: like a ship passing through billowing water, of which, when it has gone by, no trace can be found, nor the track of its keel in the waves;
verses.5:11: or as when a bird flies through the air, no proof of its course is found, but the light air, lashed by the stroke of its pinions and cloven by the force of its rushing flight, is traversed by the beating of its wings, and afterward no sign of its passage is found in it;
verses.5:12: or as when an arrow is shot at a target, the parted air immediately closes back into itself, so that one cannot discern its pathway:
verses.5:13: so we also, as soon as we were born, ceased to be, and we had no sign of virtue to show, but in our wickedness we were utterly consumed."
verses.5:14: For the hope of the ungodly is like chaff carried by the wind, and like thin frost driven by a tempest; like smoke it is dispersed by the wind, and it passes away like the remembrance of a guest who lodges for a single day.
verses.5:15: But the righteous live forever, and their reward is in the Lord, and the care of them is with the Most High.
verses.5:16: Therefore they shall receive the royal crown of splendor and the diadem of beauty from the hand of the Lord, because with His right hand He will shelter them, and with His arm He will shield them.
verses.5:17: He will take His zeal as His full armor, and will arm creation for vengeance against His enemies.
verses.5:18: He will put on righteousness as a breastplate, and wear unfeigned judgment as a helmet.
verses.5:19: He will take holiness as an invincible shield,
verses.5:20: and He will sharpen stern wrath into a sword, and the world will join Him in battle against the senseless.
verses.5:21: Well-aimed shafts of lightning will go forth, and as from a well-drawn bow of the clouds they will leap to the target,
verses.5:22: and from a catapult hailstones full of fury will be hurled; the water of the sea will rage against them, and rivers will relentlessly overwhelm them.
verses.5:23: A mighty blast will rise up against them, and like a whirlwind it will winnow them away; and all lawlessness will lay waste the earth, and evildoing will overturn the thrones of rulers.
verses.6:1: Hear therefore, O kings, and understand; learn, you judges of the ends of the earth.
verses.6:2: Give ear, you who rule over a multitude and take pride in throngs of nations.
verses.6:3: For dominion was given to you from the Lord, and sovereignty from the Most High, who will examine your works and search out your counsels.
verses.6:4: Because, though you were ministers of His kingdom, you did not judge rightly, nor did you keep the law, nor did you walk according to the counsel of God.
verses.6:5: Terribly and swiftly He will come upon you, because a stern judgment comes upon those in high places.
verses.6:6: For the lowliest man may be pardoned in mercy, but the mighty shall be mightily tested.
verses.6:7: For the Sovereign Lord of all will not shrink before anyone's presence, nor will He stand in awe of greatness; for He Himself made both small and great, and He cares for all alike.
verses.6:8: But upon the powerful a strict inquiry impends.
verses.6:9: To you therefore, O monarchs, are my words directed, that you may learn wisdom and not fall away.
verses.6:10: For those who have kept holy things in holiness shall be made holy, and those who have been taught them will find a defense.
verses.6:11: Set your desire therefore upon my words; long for them, and you shall be instructed.
verses.6:12: Radiant and unfading is wisdom, and she is readily beheld by those who love her.
verses.6:13: She anticipates those who desire her, making herself known to them first.
verses.6:14: He who rises early for her will not grow weary, for he will find her sitting beside his gates.
verses.6:15: For to reflect upon her is the perfection of understanding, and he who keeps vigil for her sake will quickly be free from anxiety.
verses.6:16: Because she herself goes about seeking those who are worthy of her, and in the pathways she graciously appears to them, and in every thought she meets them.
verses.6:17: For her truest beginning is the desire for instruction, and care for instruction is love,
verses.6:18: and love is the keeping of her laws, and giving heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption,
verses.6:19: and incorruption brings one near to God;
verses.6:20: therefore the desire for wisdom leads up to a kingdom.
verses.6:21: If therefore you delight in thrones and scepters, O monarchs of the peoples, honor wisdom, that you may reign forever.
verses.6:22: Now what wisdom is and how she came into being I will declare, and I will not hide mysteries from you; rather, I will trace her out from the beginning of creation and bring the knowledge of her into the open, and I will by no means pass by the truth.
verses.6:23: Nor indeed will I travel in company with wasting envy, because such envy will have no fellowship with wisdom.
verses.6:24: But a multitude of the wise is the salvation of the world, and a discerning king is the stability of the people.
verses.6:25: Therefore be instructed by my words, and you shall be profited.
verses.7:1: I myself also am a mortal man, equal to all others, and a descendant of the first-formed one born of the earth;
verses.7:2: and in my mother's womb I was sculpted into flesh in the space of ten months, compacted in blood from the seed of a man and the pleasure that joined with sleep.
verses.7:3: And when I was born, I also drew in the common air and fell upon the earth of like nature, uttering my first cry in weeping, just as all others do;
verses.7:4: I was nurtured in swaddling cloths and with cares.
verses.7:5: For no king had any other beginning of birth;
verses.7:6: but there is one entrance into life for all, and a like departure.
verses.7:7: Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given to me; I called out, and a spirit of wisdom came to me.
verses.7:8: I preferred her above scepters and thrones, and I counted riches as nothing in comparison with her.
verses.7:9: Neither did I liken any priceless stone to her, for all gold in her sight is a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her.
verses.7:10: I loved her above health and beauty, and I chose to have her instead of light, because the radiance from her never sleeps.
verses.7:11: Yet all good things came to me together with her, and countless wealth was in her hands;
verses.7:12: and I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom leads them, though I did not know that she was the source of them.
verses.7:13: Without guile I learned, and ungrudgingly I share; I do not conceal her riches.
verses.7:14: For she is an unfailing treasure to men, and those who make use of it gain friendship with God, being commended by the gifts that come from instruction.
verses.7:15: May God grant to me to speak with discernment and to conceive thoughts worthy of the things that have been given, for He Himself is both the guide of wisdom and the corrector of the wise.
verses.7:16: For in His hand are both we and our words, along with all understanding and skill in workmanship.
verses.7:17: For He Himself gave me unerring knowledge of the things that exist: to know the structure of the world and the working of the elements,
verses.7:18: the beginning and end and middle of times, the alternations of the solstices and the changes of the seasons,
verses.7:19: the cycles of years and the positions of the stars,
verses.7:20: the natures of living creatures and the tempers of wild beasts, the violence of winds and the reasonings of men, the varieties of plants and the powers of roots.
verses.7:21: All things, both hidden and manifest, I learned,
verses.7:22: for wisdom, the artisan of all things, taught me. For in her is a spirit that is intelligent, holy, unique, manifold, subtle, nimble, lucid, undefiled, distinct, inviolable, loving the good, keen, unhindered, beneficent,
verses.7:23: loving mankind, steadfast, sure, free from care, all-powerful, overseeing all, and penetrating through all spirits that are intelligent, pure, and most subtle.
verses.7:24: For wisdom is more mobile than any motion, and she pervades and penetrates through all things by reason of her purity.
verses.7:25: For she is a breath of the power of God, and a pure outflow of the glory of the Almighty; therefore nothing defiled steals into her.
verses.7:26: For she is a radiance of eternal light, a spotless mirror of the working of God, and an image of His goodness.
verses.7:27: And though she is one, she can do all things; and abiding in herself, she renews all things, and in every generation passing into holy souls, she makes them friends of God and prophets.
verses.7:28: For God loves no one except him who dwells with wisdom.
verses.7:29: For she is fairer than the sun, and above every constellation of the stars. Compared with light, she is found superior;
verses.7:30: for night succeeds that light, but wickedness does not prevail against wisdom.
verses.8:1: She stretches mightily from one end to the other, and she governs all things graciously.
verses.8:2: Her I loved and sought out from my youth, and I sought to take her as a bride for myself, and I became a lover of her beauty.
verses.8:3: She glorifies her noble birth by living in fellowship with God, and the Master of all has loved her;
verses.8:4: for she is an initiate into the knowledge of God, and a chooser of His works.
verses.8:5: And if wealth is a desirable possession in life, what is richer than wisdom, who works all things?
verses.8:6: And if understanding works, who more than she is the artisan of the things that exist?
verses.8:7: And if anyone loves righteousness, her labors are virtues; for she teaches self-control and prudence, righteousness and courage, and nothing in life is more profitable for men than these.
verses.8:8: And if anyone also longs for wide experience, she knows the things of old and discerns the things to come; she understands the subtleties of speeches and the solutions of riddles; she foreknows signs and wonders, and the outcomes of seasons and times.
verses.8:9: Therefore I resolved to take her to dwell with me, knowing that she would be a counselor of good things to me, and a comfort in cares and sorrow.
verses.8:10: Because of her I shall have glory among the multitudes, and honor in the presence of elders, though I am young;
verses.8:11: I shall be found keen in judgment, and in the sight of mighty men I shall be admired.
verses.8:12: When I am silent, they will wait for me; and when I speak, they will give heed; and when I speak at greater length, they will lay their hand upon their mouth.
verses.8:13: Because of her I shall have immortality, and I shall leave an everlasting remembrance to those who come after me.
verses.8:14: I shall govern peoples, and nations shall be subjected to me;
verses.8:15: dread tyrants will fear me when they hear of me; among the multitude I shall appear good, and in war courageous.
verses.8:16: When I enter my house, I shall find rest with her; for companionship with her has no bitterness, nor does living with her bring grief, but gladness and joy.
verses.8:17: When I had pondered these things within myself, and considered in my heart that in kinship with wisdom there is immortality,
verses.8:18: and in her friendship there is noble delight, and in the labors of her hands unfailing wealth, and in the discipline of her companionship understanding, and renown in the fellowship of her words, I went about seeking how I might take her to myself.
verses.8:19: Now I was a gifted child, and I received a good soul;
verses.8:20: or rather, being good, I entered an undefiled body.
verses.8:21: Yet perceiving that I would not otherwise possess her unless God gave her—and this too was a mark of understanding, to know whose gift she is—I appealed to the Lord and pleaded with Him, and I said with all my heart:
verses.9:1: "O God of the fathers and Lord of Your mercy, who made all things by Your word,
verses.9:2: and by Your wisdom formed man, that he should have dominion over the creatures that were made by You,
verses.9:3: and govern the world in holiness and righteousness, and render judgment in uprightness of soul;
verses.9:4: give me wisdom, who sits by Your thrones, and do not reject me from among Your children.
verses.9:5: For I am Your servant and the son of Your maidservant, a weak man and short-lived, and lacking in the understanding of judgment and laws.
verses.9:6: For even if someone is perfect among the sons of men, yet without the wisdom that comes from You, he shall be counted as nothing.
verses.9:7: You chose me to be king of Your people and judge of Your sons and daughters;
verses.9:8: You gave command to build a temple on Your holy mountain, and an altar in the city of Your dwelling, a copy of the holy tabernacle which You prepared beforehand from the beginning.
verses.9:9: And with You is wisdom, who knows Your works and was present when You made the world, and who understands what is pleasing in Your sight and what is right in Your commandments.
verses.9:10: Send her forth from the holy heavens, and from the throne of Your glory send her, that being present with me she may labor, and that I may know what is well-pleasing before You.
verses.9:11: For she knows and understands all things, and she shall guide me prudently in my deeds and guard me in her glory.
verses.9:12: Then my works shall be acceptable, and I shall judge Your people righteously, and I shall be worthy of the thrones of my father.
verses.9:13: For what man can know the counsel of God? Or who can conceive what the Lord wills?
verses.9:14: For the reasonings of mortals are timid, and our designs are uncertain;
verses.9:15: for a perishable body weighs down the soul, and the earthly tent burdens a mind full of cares.
verses.9:16: And we scarcely guess at the things upon earth, and what is at hand we find with labor; but the things in the heavens, who has traced out?
verses.9:17: And who has known Your counsel, unless You gave wisdom and sent Your Holy Spirit from on high?
verses.9:18: And thus the paths of those on earth were made straight, and men were taught the things that are pleasing to You, and by wisdom they were saved."
verses.10:1: She guarded the first-formed father of the world, when he was created alone, and delivered him from his own transgression,
verses.10:2: and gave him strength to have dominion over all things.
verses.10:3: But when an unrighteous man departed from her in his wrath, he perished along with his brother-slaying fury.
verses.10:4: Because of him, when the earth was overwhelmed by flood, Wisdom saved it again, steering the righteous man by means of humble wood.
verses.10:5: She also, when the nations were confounded in the accord of their wickedness, found the righteous man, preserved him blameless before God, and kept him strong against his tender affection for his child.
verses.10:6: She rescued a righteous man while the ungodly were perishing, as he fled the fire descending upon Pentapolis,
verses.10:7: as a witness to whose wickedness a smoking wasteland still stands, and plants bearing fruit in unfulfilled seasons, and a standing pillar of salt, a memorial of an unbelieving soul.
verses.10:8: For having passed by Wisdom, they not only suffered the harm of not knowing what is good, but also left to human life a memorial of their folly, so that in the things in which they stumbled they might not even escape notice.
verses.10:9: But Wisdom rescued those who served her out of their troubles.
verses.10:10: She guided a righteous man fleeing from a brother's wrath in straight paths; she showed him the kingdom of God and gave him knowledge of holy things; she prospered him in his toils and multiplied the fruits of his labors;
verses.10:11: in the greed of those who oppressed him, she stood by him and made him rich;
verses.10:12: she guarded him from enemies and kept him safe from those who lay in wait, and in a fierce contest she awarded him the victory, that he might know that godliness is mightier than all.
verses.10:13: She did not forsake a righteous man when he was sold, but delivered him from sin;
verses.10:14: she went down with him into the pit, and in bonds she did not leave him, until she brought him the scepter of a kingdom and authority over those who tyrannized him; she also exposed as liars those who accused him, and gave him everlasting glory.
verses.10:15: She delivered a holy people and a blameless seed from a nation of oppressors.
verses.10:16: She entered into the soul of a servant of the Lord, and withstood fearsome kings with wonders and signs.
verses.10:17: She gave to the holy ones the reward of their labors, guided them along a marvelous way, and became for them a shelter by day and a flame of stars through the night.
verses.10:18: She brought them across the Red Sea, and led them through deep water;
verses.10:19: but their enemies she drowned, and cast them up from the depth of the abyss.
verses.10:20: Therefore the righteous plundered the ungodly, and sang hymns to Your holy name, O Lord, and praised Your defending hand with one accord;
verses.10:21: for Wisdom opened the mouth of the mute, and made the tongues of infants articulate.
verses.11:1: She prospered their works by the hand of a holy prophet.
verses.11:2: They journeyed through an uninhabited wilderness, and pitched tents in untrodden places;
verses.11:3: they withstood foes, and repelled enemies.
verses.11:4: They thirsted and called upon You, and water was given to them from flinty rock, and a remedy for thirst from hard stone.
verses.11:5: For through the very things by which their enemies were punished, through these they themselves were benefited in their need.
verses.11:6: Whereas instead of the spring of an ever-flowing river, those were troubled with foul blood
verses.11:7: in rebuke of the infant-slaying decree, to these You gave abundant water beyond expectation,
verses.11:8: showing through the thirst of that time how You punished their adversaries.
verses.11:9: For when they were tested, though chastened in mercy, they came to know how the ungodly were tormented when judged in wrath;
verses.11:10: for these You tested as a father who admonishes, but those You scrutinized as a stern king who condemns.
verses.11:11: And whether absent or present, they were alike afflicted;
verses.11:12: for a twofold grief seized them, and a groaning over memories of things past.
verses.11:13: For when they heard that through their own punishments the others were being benefited, they perceived the Lord.
verses.11:14: For him who long ago was cast out in exposure they rejected with mockery; at the end of the events they marveled at him, having thirsted in a manner unlike the righteous.
verses.11:15: In return for the foolish reasonings of their unrighteousness, by which they were led astray to worship irrational reptiles and worthless vermin, You sent upon them a multitude of irrational creatures for vengeance,
verses.11:16: that they might know that through the very things by which one sins, through these he is punished.
verses.11:17: For Your all-powerful hand, which created the world out of formless matter, did not lack the means to send upon them a multitude of bears or fierce lions,
verses.11:18: or newly created unknown beasts full of fury, either breathing forth a fiery breath, or scattering roaring blasts of smoke, or flashing dreadful sparks from their eyes,
verses.11:19: whose harm could not only utterly crush them, but whose very sight could terrify and destroy them.
verses.11:20: Yet even apart from these, they could have fallen by a single breath, pursued by justice and scattered by the breath of Your power; but You have ordered all things by measure and number and weight.
verses.11:21: For great strength is always present with You, and who shall withstand the might of Your arm?
verses.11:22: For the whole world before You is like a slight tip of the scales, and like a drop of morning dew descending upon the earth.
verses.11:23: Yet You have mercy on all, because You can do all things, and You overlook the sins of men for the sake of repentance.
verses.11:24: For You love all things that exist, and You abhor nothing that You have made; for if You had hated anything, You would not have formed it.
verses.11:25: And how would anything have endured if You had not willed it, or how would what was not called by You have been preserved?
verses.11:26: Yet You spare all things, because they are Yours, O Sovereign Lord, lover of souls.
verses.12:1: For Your incorruptible Spirit is in all things.
verses.12:2: Therefore You reprove little by little those who fall away, and You admonish them by reminding them of the things in which they sin, that being freed from wickedness they may believe in You, O Lord.
verses.12:3: For indeed, the ancient inhabitants of Your holy land,
verses.12:4: whom You hated for practicing most hateful works of sorceries and unholy rites,
verses.12:5: both merciless murderers of children, and a feast of devourers of human inward parts, flesh, and blood, initiates from the midst of a mystic revel,
verses.12:6: and parents who were murderers of helpless souls—these You willed to destroy by the hands of our fathers,
verses.12:7: that the land most precious of all in Your sight might receive a worthy colony of the children of God.
verses.12:8: Yet even these You spared as men, and You sent wasps as forerunners of Your host, that they might destroy them little by little.
verses.12:9: Not that You were unable in battle array to deliver the ungodly into the hands of the righteous, or to wipe them out at once by fierce wild beasts or by a stern word;
verses.12:10: but judging them little by little, You gave place for repentance, not being unaware that their origin was evil and their wickedness inborn, and that their reasoning would never change forever,
verses.12:11: for they were an accursed seed from the beginning. Neither did You grant impunity for the things in which they sinned out of fear of anyone.
verses.12:12: For who shall say, "What have You done?" Or who shall withstand Your judgment? And who shall accuse You concerning the nations that perished, which You made? Or who shall come to confront You as an avenger on behalf of unrighteous men?
verses.12:13: For neither is there any god besides You, whose care is for all things, that You should show that You did not judge unrighteously;
verses.12:14: nor shall king or tyrant be able to look You in the face concerning those whom You have punished.
verses.12:15: Being righteous, You govern all things righteously, deeming it alien to Your power to condemn the one who does not deserve to be punished.
verses.12:16: For Your strength is the beginning of righteousness, and Your sovereignty over all causes You to spare all.
verses.12:17: For You show Your strength when Your perfection of power is doubted, and among those who know it You rebuke insolence.
verses.12:18: Yet You, being Sovereign over strength, judge with gentleness, and with great forbearance You govern us; for power is present with You whenever You will.
verses.12:19: And by such works You have taught Your people that the righteous man must be a lover of mankind; and You have filled Your sons with good hope, because You grant repentance for sins.
verses.12:20: For if You punished the enemies of Your children, even those deserving of death, with such great care and entreaty, granting times and place by which they might be delivered from wickedness,
verses.12:21: with how great carefulness have You judged Your sons, to whose fathers You gave oaths and covenants of good promises?
verses.12:22: Therefore, while chastening us, You scourge our enemies ten thousandfold, that when we judge we may be mindful of Your goodness, and when we are judged we may look for mercy.
verses.12:23: Consequently, You also tormented through their own abominations the unrighteous who lived in folly of life.
verses.12:24: For they went astray far beyond the paths of error, supposing to be gods those creatures that even among animals are despised by their enemies, deceived like senseless infants.
verses.12:25: Because of this, as to unreasoning children, You sent judgment as a mockery.
verses.12:26: But those who were not admonished by mocking rebukes shall experience a judgment worthy of God.
verses.12:27: For in the things through which they suffered and were indignant—being punished by these very creatures whom they supposed to be gods—they saw and recognized as the true God Him whom they had long refused to know; therefore the utmost end of condemnation also came upon them.
verses.13:1: For vain by nature were all men in whom there was ignorance of God, and from the good things that are seen they were not able to know Him who is, nor by giving heed to the works did they recognize the Craftsman.
verses.13:2: Rather, they supposed either fire, or wind, or swift air, or the circle of the stars, or violent water, or the luminaries of heaven to be gods, the rulers of the world.
verses.13:3: If, delighting in their beauty, they supposed them to be gods, let them know how much better than these is their Sovereign Master; for the First Author of beauty created them.
verses.13:4: And if they were astonished at their power and operation, let them perceive from them how much mightier is He who formed them.
verses.13:5: For from the greatness of beauty and of created things, their Creator is correspondingly beheld.
verses.13:6: Yet even so, for these men there is little blame; for perhaps they go astray while seeking God and desiring to find Him.
verses.13:7: For moving among His works they search diligently, and they are persuaded by sight, because the things that are seen are beautiful.
verses.13:8: Yet on the other hand, not even they are excusable;
verses.13:9: for if they had power to know so much that they could investigate the world, how did they not sooner find the Sovereign Master of these things?
verses.13:10: But wretched are they, and among dead things are their hopes, who called the works of men's hands gods—gold and silver, the studied work of craft, and likenesses of animals, or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand.
verses.13:11: And if a woodcutting carpenter saws down a tree easy to move, skillfully scrapes off all its bark, and fashioning it becomingly makes a useful vessel for the service of life,
verses.13:12: and uses up the scraps of his labor to prepare food and eats his fill,
verses.13:13: and takes the leftover scrap from them that is useful for nothing—a crooked piece of wood grown full of knots—and carves it with the diligence of his leisure, and shapes it by the skill of his idle hours, likening it to the image of a man,
verses.13:14: or making it resemble some worthless animal, coating it with vermilion and reddening its color with crimson dye, and coating over every blemish that is in it,
verses.13:15: and having made for it a dwelling worthy of it, sets it in a wall, securing it with iron—
verses.13:16: so then, he makes provision for it lest it fall down, knowing that it is unable to help itself; for indeed it is an image and has need of help.
verses.13:17: Yet when he prays concerning his possessions and his marriage and his children, he is not ashamed to speak to that which has no life.
verses.13:18: And for health he calls upon that which is weak; for life he petitions that which is dead; for aid he implores that which is most inexperienced; for a journey, that which cannot even take a step;
verses.13:19: and for gain, and for work, and for success of his hands, he asks capability from that which is most incapable with its hands.
verses.14:1: Again, one preparing for a voyage and about to pass through fierce waves calls upon a piece of wood more fragile than the vessel that bears him.
verses.14:2: For a desire for gain devised that vessel, and wisdom, the master artisan, built it;
verses.14:3: yet Your providence, O Father, steers it, for You have given a way even in the sea and a safe path among the waves,
verses.14:4: showing that You are able to save from all things, so that even without skill one may embark.
verses.14:5: Yet You desire that the works of Your wisdom should not be idle; therefore men entrust their lives even to the slightest piece of wood, and passing through the surging waves on a raft, they are brought safely through.
verses.14:6: For in the beginning also, when the proud giants were perishing, the hope of the world took refuge upon a raft, and being steered by Your hand, left to the age a seed of a new generation.
verses.14:7: For blessed is the wood through which righteousness comes;
verses.14:8: but what is made by hands is accursed, both it and the one who made it—because he indeed fashioned it, while the perishable thing was named a god.
verses.14:9: For both the ungodly man and his ungodliness are equally hateful to God;
verses.14:10: for indeed the thing made shall be punished together with the one who made it.
verses.14:11: Therefore upon the idols of the nations also there shall be a visitation, because within the creation of God they have become an abomination, and stumbling blocks to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the foolish.
verses.14:12: For the devising of idols was the beginning of fornication, and the inventions of them were the corruption of life.
verses.14:13: For neither did they exist from the beginning, nor shall they remain forever;
verses.14:14: for by the vainglory of men they entered into the world, and therefore a swift end has been devised for them.
verses.14:15: For a father, worn down by untimely grief, having made an image of the child swiftly taken away, now honored as a god one who was then a dead mortal, and handed down to those under his authority mysteries and rites;
verses.14:16: then in the course of time the ungodly custom grew strong and was kept as a law,
verses.14:17: and by the commands of tyrants graven images were worshiped. When men could not honor them face to face because they dwelt far away, they pictured their distant likeness and made a visible image of the king whom they honored, that by their zeal they might flatter the absent one as though he were present.
verses.14:18: Moreover, the ambition of the craftsman spurred on even those who did not know him to greater intensity of worship.
verses.14:19: For he, wishing perhaps to please the ruler, forced the likeness by his skill into greater beauty;
verses.14:20: and the multitude, drawn by the grace of the workmanship, now reckoned as an object of worship the man who a short time before had been honored.
verses.14:21: And this became a hidden snare for human life, because men, enslaved either to calamity or to tyranny, bestowed upon stones and wood the incommunicable Name.
verses.14:22: Then it was not enough that they erred concerning the knowledge of God, but living also in a great war of ignorance, they call such great evils peace.
verses.14:23: For while celebrating either child-murdering rites, or secret mysteries, or frenzied revelries of strange ordinances,
verses.14:24: they no longer keep either lives or marriages pure, but one man either lies in ambush and slays another, or grieves him by adultery.
verses.14:25: And all is mingled together in confusion—blood and murder, theft and deceit, corruption, faithlessness, tumult, perjury,
verses.14:26: troubling of the good, forgetfulness of kindness, defilement of souls, confusion of nature, disorder in marriages, adultery, and licentiousness.
verses.14:27: For the worship of nameless idols is the beginning, cause, and end of every evil;
verses.14:28: for either they are mad in their reveling, or they prophesy falsehoods, or they live unrighteously, or they swiftly swear falsely;
verses.14:29: for trusting in lifeless idols, they do not expect to suffer harm when they have sworn falsely.
verses.14:30: Yet just retribution shall overtake them on both counts, because they thought falsely concerning God in giving heed to idols, and they swore unrighteously in deceit, despising holiness.
verses.14:31: For it is not the power of the things sworn by, but the justice upon sinners that always pursues the transgression of the unrighteous.
verses.15:1: But You, our God, are gracious and true, longsuffering, and governing all things in mercy.
verses.15:2: For even if we sin, we are Yours, knowing Your might; we will not sin, knowing that we are counted as Yours.
verses.15:3: For to know You is complete righteousness, and to know Your might is the root of immortality.
verses.15:4: For neither has the mischievous invention of men led us astray, nor the fruitless labor of painters, a figure stained with varied colors,
verses.15:5: the sight of which brings reproach upon fools, as one longs for the breathless form of a dead image.
verses.15:6: Lovers of evil things and worthy of such hopes are both those who make them, and those who long for them, and those who worship them.
verses.15:7: For a potter also, laboriously pressing soft earth, molds each vessel for our service; yet out of the same clay he fashions both the vessels that serve clean uses and those for the contrary, all alike; but what the use of each of either sort shall be, the worker in clay is the judge.
verses.15:8: And with misspent toil he molds a vain god out of the same clay—he who a little while before was made from earth, and after a little while returns to that from which he was taken, when the debt of his soul is required of him.
verses.15:9: Yet his concern is not that he is about to fail, nor that he has a fleeting life, but he competes with goldsmiths and silversmiths, and imitates workers in bronze, and counts it a glory that he molds counterfeits.
verses.15:10: His heart is ashes, and his hope is of less worth than earth, and his life is of less honor than clay,
verses.15:11: because he did not know Him who formed him, and who inspired into him an active soul and breathed into him a life-giving spirit;
verses.15:12: Instead, he reckoned our life to be a sport and our existence a festival for gain; for, he says, one must make profit from every source, even from evil.
verses.15:13: For this man above all others knows that he sins, fashioning out of earthy matter fragile vessels and graven images.
verses.15:14: Yet most foolish of all, and more wretched than the soul of an infant, are all the enemies of Your people who oppressed them.
verses.15:15: For they also reckoned all the idols of the nations to be gods, which have neither the use of eyes to see, nor nostrils to draw in air, nor ears to hear, nor fingers on their hands to feel, and their feet are helpless for walking.
verses.15:16: For a man made them, and one whose spirit is borrowed molded them; for no man is able to mold a god like himself.
verses.15:17: Being mortal, he makes a dead thing with lawless hands; for he is better than the objects of his worship, since he indeed lived, whereas they never did.
verses.15:18: Moreover, they worship even the most hateful beasts; for when compared in senselessness, they are worse than the others.
verses.15:19: Nor are they even so fair in their appearance among living creatures as to be desired, but they have escaped both the praise of God and His blessing.
verses.16:1: Therefore they were deservedly punished through like things, and through a multitude of noxious creatures they were tormented.
verses.16:2: Instead of that punishment, You showed kindness to Your people, and for the longing of their appetite You prepared an unusual delicacy, quail for food,
verses.16:3: so that the former, though desiring food, might turn away even from their necessary appetite because of the sight displayed of the creatures sent upon them, while the latter, having been in want for a little while, might partake even of an unusual delicacy.
verses.16:4: For it was necessary that relentless want should come upon those who acted as tyrants, but to these it should only be shown how their enemies were tormented.
verses.16:5: For even when the fierce fury of wild beasts came upon them, and they were perishing by the bites of writhing serpents, Your wrath did not continue to the end.
verses.16:6: Instead, they were troubled for a little while as an admonition, having a token of salvation as a reminder of the commandment of Your law;
verses.16:7: for the one who turned to look was not saved by the thing beheld, but by You, the Savior of all.
verses.16:8: And by this also You convinced our enemies that You are the One who delivers from every evil.
verses.16:9: For the bites of locusts and flies slew them, and no healing was found for their life, because they were worthy to be punished by such creatures;
verses.16:10: but not even the fangs of venomous serpents conquered Your sons, for Your mercy intervened and healed them.
verses.16:11: For they were stung to remind them of Your oracles, and swiftly rescued, lest falling into deep forgetfulness they should become unmindful of Your kindness.
verses.16:12: For neither herb nor poultice cured them, but Your word, O Lord, which heals all things.
verses.16:13: For You have authority over life and death; You lead down to the gates of Hades and bring up again.
verses.16:14: A man indeed slays in his malice, yet he does not bring back the spirit that has gone forth, nor does he release a soul once taken away.
verses.16:15: Yet it is impossible to escape Your hand.
verses.16:16: For the ungodly who refused to know You were scourged by the strength of Your arm, pursued by strange rains and hail and relentless downpours, and consumed by fire.
verses.16:17: For most wondrous of all, in the water that quenches all things the fire raged all the more fiercely, for the world is the defender of the righteous.
verses.16:18: For at one time the flame was tamed, so that it would not burn up the living creatures sent against the ungodly, but that seeing this they themselves might know that they were pursued by the judgment of God;
verses.16:19: and at another time, even in the midst of water, it blazes beyond the power of fire, to destroy the produce of an unrighteous land.
verses.16:20: Instead of these things, You fed Your people with the food of angels, and without toil You sent them bread made ready from heaven, able to yield every delight and suited to every taste.
verses.16:21: For Your sustenance manifested Your sweetness toward Your children; and serving the desire of him who partook of it, it was transformed into whatever each one wished.
verses.16:22: Now snow and ice endured fire and did not melt, so that they might know that fire, blazing in the hail and flashing through the rains, was destroying the crops of the enemies;
verses.16:23: yet this same fire, on the other hand, so that the righteous might be nourished, has forgotten even its own power.
verses.16:24: For creation, serving You who made it, strains itself for punishment against the unrighteous, and relaxes into kindness on behalf of those who trust in You.
verses.16:25: Therefore even then, transformed into all things, it ministered to Your all-nourishing bounty according to the wish of those in need,
verses.16:26: so that Your sons, whom You loved, O Lord, might learn that it is not the yielding of crops that nourishes man, but Your word preserves those who trust in You.
verses.16:27: For what was not destroyed by fire simply melted when warmed by a fleeting ray of the sun,
verses.16:28: so that it might be known that one must rise before the sun to give thanks to You, and pray to You at the dawning of the light.
verses.16:29: For the hope of the ungrateful will melt away like wintry frost, and will flow away like useless water.
verses.17:1: For great are Your judgments and hard to describe; therefore uninstructed souls went astray.
verses.17:2: For when lawless men supposed that they oppressed a holy nation, they themselves—prisoners of darkness and captives fettered by a long night, shut in beneath their roofs—lay exiled from eternal providence.
verses.17:3: For thinking that they were hidden in their secret sins, they were scattered beneath a dark veil of forgetfulness, terribly dismayed and deeply troubled by apparitions.
verses.17:4: For not even the inner chamber that held them kept them free from fear; terrifying sounds resounded around them, and gloomy specters with unsmiling faces appeared.
verses.17:5: No force of fire had power to give light, nor did the brilliant flames of the stars endure to illuminate that dismal night.
verses.17:6: Only a self-kindled blaze full of terror shone through to them, and terrified by that unseen apparition, they deemed the things they saw to be even worse.
verses.17:7: The illusions of magic art lay defeated, and their boast of wisdom received a humiliating rebuke;
verses.17:8: for those who promised to drive away terrors and disorders from a sick soul were themselves sick with a laughable dread.
verses.17:9: For even if nothing dreadful frightened them, yet startled by the passing of noxious creatures and the hissing of reptiles, they perished in trembling, refusing even to look upon the air, which cannot on any side be escaped.
verses.17:10: For wickedness, being condemned, bears witness by its own nature that it is cowardly, and pressed hard by conscience it always imagines the worst.
verses.17:11: For fear is nothing other than the surrender of the aids that come from reason;
verses.17:12: and the weaker the expectation from within, the heavier it counts ignorance of the cause that brings the torment.
verses.17:13: But throughout that truly powerless night, which had come upon them from the recesses of powerless Hades, sleeping the same sleep,
verses.17:14: at one moment they were driven by monstrous apparitions, and at another they were paralyzed by the surrender of their soul; for a sudden and unexpected terror came upon them.
verses.17:15: Thus, whoever fell down there was kept under guard, shut up in that prison without iron bars;
verses.17:16: for whether a man was a farmer, or a shepherd, or a laborer toiling in the wilderness, he was overtaken and endured that inescapable necessity.
verses.17:17: For with one chain of darkness they were all bound. Whether it was a whistling wind, or the melodious sound of birds among spreading branches, or the rhythm of water rushing with force, or the harsh crash of tumbling rocks,
verses.17:18: or the unseen running of bounding animals, or the voice of the fiercest roaring beasts, or an echo rebounding from the hollows of the mountains—these terrified and paralyzed them.
verses.17:19: For the whole world was illuminated with brilliant light and continued in unhindered labors;
verses.17:20: over them alone was spread a heavy night, an image of the darkness that was about to receive them; yet to themselves they were heavier than the darkness.
verses.18:1: Yet for Your holy ones there was a very great light. Hearing their voice, yet not seeing their form, they counted them blessed because they also had suffered;
verses.18:2: and because they did them no harm, though they had been wronged before, they gave thanks, and asked pardon for having been at variance with them.
verses.18:3: In return for these things, You provided a blazing pillar of fire, a guide for an unknown journey, and a harmless sun for their honorable sojourn.
verses.18:4: For they indeed were worthy to be deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness, who had kept Your sons shut up in confinement, through whom the imperishable light of the law was to be given to the world.
verses.18:5: When they had plotted to slay the infants of the holy ones, and a single child was cast out and saved, for their reproof You took away the multitude of their own children, and destroyed them all together in violent water.
verses.18:6: That night was made known beforehand to our fathers, so that, knowing with certainty the oaths in which they had trusted, they might be of good cheer.
verses.18:7: The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of their enemies were awaited by Your people.
verses.18:8: For just as You punished the adversaries, by that very means You called us to Yourself and glorified us.
verses.18:9: For in secret the holy children of good men were offering sacrifice, and with one accord they ordained the divine law, that the saints would share alike in the same blessings and the same perils, while the fathers were already singing beforehand the hymns of praise.
verses.18:10: Yet the discordant cry of their enemies echoed back, and a pitiful wail was borne abroad for the children being lamented.
verses.18:11: With a like penalty the servant was punished together with his master, and the commoner suffered the same things as the king;
verses.18:12: and all together, under one name of death, had dead without number; for the living were not even sufficient to bury them, since in a single moment their noblest offspring was destroyed.
verses.18:13: For though they disbelieved all things because of their sorceries, at the destruction of the firstborn they confessed that this people was God's son.
verses.18:14: For while peaceful silence encompassed all things, and night in its own swift course was midway through all things,
verses.18:15: Your all-powerful word leaped from the heavens, out of the royal throne, a stern warrior into the midst of the doomed land, bearing as a sharp sword Your unfeigned command,
verses.18:16: and standing, filled all things with death; it touched heaven, yet stood upon the earth.
verses.18:17: Then at once visions of dreams dreadfully troubled them, and unexpected terrors came upon them,
verses.18:18: and one here and another there, cast down half-dead, declared the reason for which he was dying;
verses.18:19: for the dreams that troubled them had forewarned them of this, lest they perish without knowing why they were suffering so grievously.
verses.18:20: Yet the experience of death touched the righteous also, and a plague came upon the multitude in the wilderness; but the wrath did not abide for long.
verses.18:21: For a blameless man made haste to stand in their defense, bringing the weapon of his own ministry—prayer and the atonement of incense; he withstood the fury and put an end to the calamity, showing that he is Your servant.
verses.18:22: He overcame the turmoil not by strength of body, nor by force of arms, but by a word he subdued the one who was punishing, calling to remembrance the oaths and covenants of the fathers.
verses.18:23: For when the dead had already fallen in heaps one upon another, he stood between and beat back the wrath, and cut off its way to the living.
verses.18:24: For upon his full-length robe was the whole world, and the glories of the fathers were upon the four rows of carved stones, and Your majesty was upon the diadem of his head.
verses.18:25: To these the destroyer yielded, and these they feared; for the mere trial of the wrath was sufficient.
verses.19:1: But upon the ungodly merciless wrath came even to the end; for He knew beforehand even what they were yet to do,
verses.19:2: that after they themselves had consented for them to depart and had sent them away in haste, they would change their minds and pursue them.
verses.19:3: For while they still had their mourning in hand and were lamenting at the graves of the dead, they took up another foolish purpose, and those whom they had driven out with pleas, these they pursued as fugitives.
verses.19:4: For a deserved necessity was drawing them to this end, and cast upon them forgetfulness of the things that had befallen them, so that they might fill up the punishment that was still lacking to their torments,
verses.19:5: and that Your people might experience a wondrous journey, while those others might find a strange death.
verses.19:6: For the whole creation in its own kind was fashioned anew from the beginning, serving its own commands, so that Your children might be kept unharmed.
verses.19:7: The cloud overshadowing the camp, and the emergence of dry land out of water that stood before, were beheld—an unhindered way out of the Red Sea, and a grass-bearing plain out of a violent surge;
verses.19:8: through which they passed as a whole nation, sheltered by Your hand, beholding marvelous wonders.
verses.19:9: For like horses they ranged at pasture, and like lambs they leaped about, praising You, O Lord, who delivered them;
verses.19:10: for they still remembered the events of their sojourn, how instead of producing animals the earth brought forth gnats, and instead of aquatic creatures the river poured forth a multitude of frogs.
verses.19:11: And afterward they saw also a new generation of birds, when, led on by desire, they asked for delicacies;
verses.19:12: for to comfort them, quail came up for them from the sea,
verses.19:13: and punishments came upon the sinners, not without earlier tokens by the force of thunderbolts; for justly they suffered for their own wicked deeds, because they practiced a more grievous hatred of strangers.
verses.19:14: For the others did not receive unknown visitors when they arrived, whereas these enslaved guests who were their benefactors.
verses.19:15: And not only so, but surely there shall be some visitation for them, since they received foreigners with hostility;
verses.19:16: whereas these, after welcoming with festivities those who had already shared in the same rights, afflicted them with grievous toils.
verses.19:17: They also were struck with blindness, just as those were at the doors of the righteous man, when, enveloped in fathomless darkness, each one sought the passage through his own doors.
verses.19:18: For the elements changed harmony among themselves, just as on a harp the notes alter the name of the rhythm while always abiding in sound—which may be accurately inferred from beholding the things that came to pass.
verses.19:19: For land creatures were changed into creatures of the water, and swimming creatures crossed over upon the land;
verses.19:20: fire prevailed in water beyond its own power, and water forgot its quenching power;
verses.19:21: flames, on the contrary, did not consume the flesh of perishable living creatures walking among them, nor the melting, easily dissolved, ice-like kind of immortal food.
verses.19:22: For in all things, O Lord, You magnified Your people and glorified them, and did not neglect them, standing by them in every time and place.

notes.1:5: Greek ἐλεγχθήσεται literally means "will be put to shame" or "convicted," here conveying that the holy spirit of discipline is repelled and will not abide when unrighteousness approaches.
notes.1:14: Greek γενέσεις can mean "generations," "creatures," or "generative forces" of the world.
notes.1:16: The pronouns "him" and "his" refer back to personified Death (vv. 12–13), with v. 15 standing as a parenthetical statement.
notes.2:7: The Greek text reads ἄνθος ἀέρος ("flower of the air"); some manuscripts and emendations read ἄνθος ἔαρος ("flower of spring").
notes.2:13: Greek παῖδα can mean either "child" or "servant" of the Lord.
notes.2:22: The verse division splits the Greek phrase μυστήρια αὐτοῦ ("the mysteries of Him," referring to God); some manuscripts read θεοῦ ("of God") instead of αὐτοῦ.
notes.2:23: The Greek text reads ἰδιότητος ("nature" or "proper being"); some manuscripts read ἀϊδιότητος ("eternity").
notes.3:9: Some manuscripts add "and visitation is upon His holy ones" at the end of the verse, which is absent from the Greek text translated here.
notes.3:14: Greek τῆς πίστεως χάρις ἐκλεκτή ("a choice favor for his faithfulness") echoes the promise to faithful eunuchs in Isaiah 56:4–5.
notes.3:18: Greek διάγνωσις denotes a formal judicial examination or verdict ("day of decision").
notes.4:6: Greek literally reads "children born of unlawful sleeps," an idiom for illicit sexual unions.
notes.4:10: An unnamed allusion to Enoch, who was well-pleasing to God and was taken away by Him (Genesis 5:24 LXX).
notes.4:14: The verb may be taken intransitively ("it/he hastened out," with his soul or the righteous man as subject) or transitively ("He hurried him out," with the Lord as subject).
notes.4:19: In this critical text, traditional verse 4:18 is combined into 4:19, so 4:18 does not appear as a separate verse.
notes.5:14: This critical text reads "frost" (pachne), whereas some manuscripts read "spray" or "foam" (achne).
notes.5:23: This critical text reads nominative "all" (pasa) modifying "lawlessness," whereas other witnesses read accusative "all" (pasan) modifying "the earth."
notes.6:9: Greek tyrannoi here refers to absolute sovereigns or monarchs rather than carrying a strictly pejorative sense.
notes.6:12: This critical text does not include the clause "and is found by those who seek her" that appears in some other editions.
notes.6:17: Verses 6:17-20 form a classical Greek sorites (chain argument), linking the desire for instruction step by step to royal dominion.
notes.7:2: Ancient Mediterranean reckoning commonly counted human gestation as ten lunar months.
notes.7:3: The Greek adjective homoiopathes ("of like nature" or "sharing the same lot") suggests either the earth's shared condition with mortals or its impartial reception of all alike.
notes.7:12: The Greek noun genesis means "origin" or "source," later rendered "mother" in the Latin Vulgate.
notes.7:20: The Greek pneumaton may mean either "winds" (fitting the natural-science catalog) or "spirits" (paired with human reasonings).
notes.8:7: These four virtues—self-control, prudence, righteousness, and courage—represent the classical Hellenistic canon of the four cardinal virtues.
notes.8:19: Verses 19–20 use Hellenistic-Jewish philosophical phrasing regarding the soul's goodness in relation to the body, while affirming in verse 20 that the body itself is undefiled.
notes.8:21: Greek enkrates here denotes "having possession of" wisdom, though in other contexts it can mean "self-controlled."
notes.9:1: The Greek text literally reads "Lord of Your mercy" (Kyrie tou eleous sou), retaining the possessive pronoun attested in major Septuagint witnesses.
notes.9:4: The Greek uses the plural "Your thrones" (paralleled by "the thrones of my father" in verse 12), and paidon ("children") may also be rendered "servants."
notes.9:15: The metaphor of the perishable body as an "earthly tent" weighing down the soul draws on Hellenistic philosophical idiom to express mortal limitation rather than an inherently evil body.
notes.10:6: Pentapolis (literally 'Five Cities') is the Greek proper name used here for the five cities of the plain—Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Zoar (Genesis 14:2; 19:24–25).
notes.10:10: Greek hagion may be understood either as neuter ('holy things') or masculine ('holy ones,' i.e., angels), alluding to Jacob's vision at Bethel (Genesis 28:12–17).
notes.10:12: The 'fierce contest' alludes to Jacob's wrestling at the Jabbok (Genesis 32:24–30), employing athletic imagery (ebrabeusen, 'awarded the prize').
notes.11:6: The Greek text has the masculine plural participle tarachthentes ('troubled'), an abrupt construction referring to the Egyptians in contrast with Israel in verse 7; some manuscripts read the genitive singular tarachthentos, modifying 'river.'
notes.11:14: Alludes to Moses, who was exposed in a basket on the Nile (Exodus 2:3) and later mocked before Pharaoh, yet finally held in awe by the Egyptians.
notes.11:17: The phrase 'out of formless matter' (ex amorphou hyles) draws on Hellenistic philosophical terminology echoing the unformed earth of Genesis 1:2 LXX.
notes.11:26: Greek philopsyche means 'lover of souls' or 'lover of life,' a rare epithet applied here to God as the compassionate preserver of all living beings.
notes.12:5: The Greek syntax is unusually compressed; "a feast of devourers of human inward parts, flesh, and blood" reflects the rare compound splanchnophagon ("entrail-devourers") with thoinan ("feast"), describing cannibalistic mystery rites (mystas thiasou).
notes.12:20: Translates the Greek text deeseos ("entreaty"), attested in major manuscripts; some modern critical editions emend the word to dieseos ("indulgence" or "remission").
notes.12:24: The Greek phrase ta kai en zoois ton echthron atima is grammatically ambiguous and may also be understood as "the most despised even among hostile animals."
notes.13:1: The Greek expression ton onta ("Him who is") echoes the Septuagint rendering of the divine name in Exodus 3:14 (ho on, "He who is").
notes.13:5: Follows the Greek text megethous kallones kai ktismaton ("greatness of beauty and of created things"); other manuscripts and editions read megethous kai kallones ktismaton ("greatness and beauty of created things").
notes.13:13: Preserves the Greek oxymoronic pairing en epimeleia argias ("with the diligence of his leisure") and empeiria aneseos ("by the skill of his idle hours"); some witnesses alter aneseos ("relaxation/ease") to syneseos ("understanding").
notes.14:6: An allusion to Noah's ark as a raft preserving humanity during the Flood, when the giants (Genesis 6:4 LXX) perished.
notes.14:21: The "incommunicable Name" (Greek to akoinoneton onoma) refers to the unique divine Name that belongs to God alone and cannot be shared with any creature.
notes.14:26: "Confusion of nature" (Greek geneseos enallage) literally means an interchange of kind or origin, variously understood as unnatural sexual practices or the confounding of human lineage.
notes.14:27: "Nameless idols" (Greek anonymon eidolon) denotes idols unworthy to be named, contrasting with the incommunicable Name of God in verse 21.
notes.15:5: The Greek text reads oneidos ("reproach"), followed here; some commentators conjecture orexin ("desire" or "lust") to match "longs for" in the second clause.
notes.15:7: The image of the potter shaping vessels for clean and contrary uses from the same clay echoes Jeremiah 18 and anticipates Paul's illustration in Romans 9:21.
notes.15:14: The critique turns here to the Egyptians, the oppressors of Israel, whose animal worship is condemned in verses 18-19.
notes.15:19: This contrasts the despised creatures worshiped in Egypt with Genesis 1:21-25, where God declared the animals He created good and blessed them.
notes.16:3: The Greek phrase literally reads "because of the [one] shown of those sent upon them," with a feminine noun such as "appearance" or "sight" implied; some critics conjecture the similar-looking noun aeideian ("loathsomeness").
notes.16:11: Greek aperispastoi literally means "undistracted" or "unconcerned," used here with the genitive to mean becoming unresponsive to or unmindful of God's kindness.
notes.16:21: Greek hypostasis here means "sustenance" (referring to the manna provided by God), though the term can also denote "substance" or "nature."
notes.17:6: The Greek phrase "that unseen apparition" (or "that sight no longer seen") conveys that in their terror over what they could not clearly discern, the Egyptians imagined the things they did see to be even worse.
notes.17:10: The critical Greek text reads idios ... martyrei ("bears witness by its own nature"), whereas some manuscripts read idio ... martyri ("condemned by its own witness"). The verb proseliphen ("imagines") literally means "has always taken on" or "added" grievous things.
notes.17:12: The compressed Greek clause may be construed either with "of the cause" as an objective genitive ("counts ignorance of the cause that brings the torment heavier") or as a genitive of comparison ("counts ignorance worse than the cause that brings the torment").
notes.18:1: The Greek text lacks the negative particle "not" (reading literally "because they also had suffered"), referring to Israel's earlier affliction; some later witnesses and editors insert "not" to read "because they had not suffered as well."
notes.18:14: The Greek text repeats "all things" at the end of the clause ("was midway through all things"), whereas some manuscripts omit the second occurrence.
notes.18:22: The Greek text reads "the turmoil" (Greek ochlon, which can also mean "the multitude"); many commentators emend the word to cholon ("the anger" or "wrath").
notes.18:25: The Greek shifts from the singular "the destroyer" to the plural verb "they feared," apparently viewing the instruments of destruction collectively; some manuscripts smooth this to the singular "he feared."
notes.19:5: Replaces literal Greek-to-English bare demonstrative 'those' with idiomatic 'those others' to preserve the μὲν...δέ / ἐκεῖνοι contrast cleanly in modern NKJV English.
notes.19:6: The Greek text reads "serving its own commands" (the ordinances appointed to creation), whereas some witnesses and editions read "Your commands."
notes.19:15: The sense of "visitation" (Greek episkope) here is debated: it may mean either that Sodom will face some divine judgment for its hostility or that Sodom will receive some measure of consideration compared with Egypt's greater treachery in verse 16.
notes.19:18: Literally "alter the name of the rhythm while always abiding in sound," a musical analogy describing how the physical elements keep their underlying substance while being transposed to produce new miraculous effects.
notes.19:21: The Greek text reads the double adjective "melting, easily dissolved" (tekton eutekton) governed by "did not consume"; some witnesses read the verb etekon ("nor did they melt") in place of tekton.
